items.title: Stable regularly tempered classical positional preparation
items.statement:
Fix an integer spatial dimension $d\geq1$, a reference length $\ell_0>0$ measured in metres, and a bounded Lebesgue-measurable region $\Lambda\subset\mathbb R^d$ with dimensionless volume $V=|\Lambda|<\infty$. Its physical region is $\ell_0\Lambda$. The coordinate $x\in\Lambda$ is dimensionless and represents physical position $\ell_0x$. Use the Euclidean norm $|x|_2=(\sum_{j=1}^d x_j^2)^{1/2}$ and the maximum norm $|x|_\infty=\max_{1\leq j\leq d}|x_j|$. A finite positional configuration of $N$ classical point particles in $\Lambda$ is an unordered simple set $\omega=\{x_1,\ldots,x_N\}\subset\Lambda$; simple means that no point is repeated. Particle number $N$ is a dimensionless nonnegative integer. When $V>0$, the physical number density corresponding to the dimensionless density $N/V$ is $N/(\ell_0^dV)$, in $\mathrm{m}^{-d}$; no density $N/V$ is assigned when $V=0$.

A pair potential is an even measurable function $\varphi:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$, where $\varphi(x)$ is the interaction energy in joules at physical displacement $\ell_0x$ and evenness means $\varphi(x)=\varphi(-x)$. Set $E_0=1\,\mathrm J$ and $\widehat\varphi=\varphi/E_0$. Whenever $\widehat\varphi$ is Borel measurable, it is the dimensionless numerical potential used by [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]. For a labelled representative of $\omega$, define the positional pair energy
$$H_N(\omega)=\sum_{1\leq i<j\leq N}\varphi(x_i-x_j),\qquad H_0=H_1=0.$$
If any pair is forbidden by the potential, its energy and hence $H_N$ are $+\infty$. This model contains no kinetic energy, internal molecular coordinates, quantum exchange terms, or external field.

The interaction is stable if there is a constant $B\geq0$, measured in joules, such that $H_N(\omega)\geq-BN$ for every finite simple configuration. It has a regular integrable tail if there are $R>0$ and a nonnegative nonincreasing measurable function $\psi:[R,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$, measured in joules, such that $|\varphi(x)|\leq\psi(|x|_2)$ for $|x|_2\geq R$ and
$$\int_R^\infty r^{d-1}\psi(r)\,dr<\infty.$$
A stable potential with this tail condition is the stable regularly tempered class used for the free-cube results on this page. Superstability and a positive divergent core are stronger, separate hypotheses and are not implied by stability.

At temperature $T>0$ measured in kelvins, use the exact SI Boltzmann constant $k_{\mathrm B}=1.380649\times10^{-23}\,\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$ of [[def-td-si-quantities]] and write $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$ in joules inverse. Thus $\beta H_N$ is dimensionless. The activity $z>0$ is dimensionless relative to the reference intensity $\ell_0^{-d}$. A free-wall finite-volume model contains only positions in $\Lambda$ and uses $H_N$ above.

For periodic boundary conditions, identify a cubic cell of side $L$ in these dimensionless coordinates with the torus $\mathbb R^d/(L\mathbb Z^d)$. For its half-open representative $\Lambda_L=[0,L)^d$ and a finite simple configuration $\omega\subset\Lambda_L$, define the periodic continuation $\omega^{\mathrm{per}}=\{x+Lk:x\in\omega,\ k\in\mathbb Z^d\}$ and
$$H_{L,\mathrm{per}}(\omega)=\frac12\sum_{x\in\omega}\sum_{\substack{y\in\omega^{\mathrm{per}}\\ y\ne x}}\varphi(y-x).$$
Here the inner sum omits only the identical point $y=x$; it includes images of the same particle in other cells. The factor $1/2$ removes double counting of ordered representatives of each periodic pair. For any fixed $L>0$ and finite $\omega$, the $|k|_\infty=m$ image shell has $O_d(m^{d-1})$ terms and, outside finitely many $m$, $|y-x+Lk|_2\geq (L/2)m$. Monotonicity and the finite weighted tail integral imply $\sum_m m^{d-1}\psi(Lm/2)<\infty$, so the far-image tail is absolutely convergent. The remaining near-image set is finite; a term $+\infty$ makes $H_{L,\mathrm{per}}=+\infty$, and otherwise the finite near terms plus the absolutely convergent tail define the sum. Translating a centered half-open cell to $[0,L)^d$ preserves every displacement and this energy. Free-wall and periodic preparations are distinct boundary conditions. All limits on this page concern positional configurations and do not by themselves include a momentum integral or a full phase-space energy shell.

items.physical_scope: Nonrelativistic classical point-particle models whose thermodynamic claims concern positions and pair interactions; kinetic momentum variables are outside this definition.

items.title: Van Hove regions and uniformly tempered exterior preparations
items.statement:
Use the dimensionless coordinates, simple configurations, and pair potential of [[def-td-stable-tempered-continuum-preparation]], with $d\geq2$ as stated in this physical scope. The boundary $\partial\Lambda$ is the topological boundary in the Euclidean topology of $\mathbb R^d$, and $\operatorname{dist}(x,\partial\Lambda)=\inf_{y\in\partial\Lambda}|x-y|_2$. For a bounded measurable region $\Lambda$, define its two-sided layer of width $s>0$ by
$$\partial_s\Lambda=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:\operatorname{dist}(x,\partial\Lambda)\leq s\}.$$
A sequence $(\Lambda_k)_{k\geq1}$ of bounded measurable regions is van Hove if $0<|\Lambda_k|<\infty$, $|\Lambda_k|\to\infty$, and, for every fixed $s>0$,
$$\frac{|\partial_s\Lambda_k|}{|\Lambda_k|}\longrightarrow0.$$
This is the two-sided Euclidean boundary-layer condition used by the mathematical shape suppliers; it controls points on both sides of $\partial\Lambda_k$. Increasing volume alone does not imply it. A free wall permits particles only in $\Lambda_k$ and includes no exterior particles. A periodic wall uses the specified periodic cell and its image convention.

For the deterministic exterior class, let $C=[-1/2,1/2)^d$ and $\Lambda_n=[-n-1/2,n+1/2)^d$, with dimensionless volume $V_n=|\Lambda_n|$. A configuration $\zeta\subset\mathbb R^d$ is locally finite if $|\zeta\cap K|<\infty$ for every bounded set $K\subset\mathbb R^d$. For such $\zeta$, write $N_{C+i}(\zeta)=|\zeta\cap(C+i)|$. The parameter $t$ is dimensionless. Given $0\leq t<\infty$, define
$$\Omega(t)=\left\{\zeta:\sum_{i\in\Lambda_n\cap\mathbb Z^d}N_{C+i}(\zeta)^2\leq tV_n\ \text{for every integer }n\geq0\right\}.$$
For an interior finite configuration $\omega\subset\Lambda_n$ and $\zeta\in\Omega(t)$, its exterior interaction is
$$W_n(\omega,\zeta)=\sum_{x\in\omega}\sum_{y\in\zeta\setminus\Lambda_n}\varphi(x-y).$$
This sum is well-defined in $\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$. Indeed, Cauchy--Schwarz and the defining bound for $\Omega(t)$ give $|\zeta\cap\Lambda_m|\leq\sqrt t\,V_m=O_t(m^d)$. Since $\omega$ is finite and bounded, for each fixed $x\in\omega$ and all sufficiently large dyadic shells $2^k\leq |y|_2<2^{k+1}$, one has $|x-y|_2\geq c2^k$ for some $c>0$. The absolute interaction on that shell is at most a constant times $2^{kd}\psi(c2^k)$. These bounds are summable: monotonicity gives $\int_{c2^{k-1}}^{c2^k}r^{d-1}\psi(r)\,dr\geq C_d2^{kd}\psi(c2^k)$ for a constant $C_d>0$, and the tail integral is finite. Only finitely many near exterior points remain; if one contributes $+\infty$, set $W_n=+\infty$, and otherwise the near sum and absolutely convergent tail define $W_n$. A positive infinite value has zero Boltzmann weight. The class $\Omega(t)$ is a fixed uniform bound on exterior cell counts, not permission for an arbitrary volume-filling external potential. The van Hove and uniformly tempered exterior conditions are separate boundary regimes.

items.physical_scope: Classical positional pair-potential models in dimension d at least two, with free walls, periodic walls, or the explicitly bounded deterministic exterior class defined here.

items.title: Indistinguishable-particle positional measure
items.statement:
Let $\Lambda\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a bounded Lebesgue-measurable region in the dimensionless coordinates of [[def-td-stable-tempered-continuum-preparation]]. Use the completed product-Lebesgue sigma-algebra on $\Lambda^N$. For $N\geq1$, let
$$D_{\Lambda,N}=\{(x_1,\ldots,x_N)\in\Lambda^N:x_i\ne x_j\text{ whenever }i\ne j\},\qquad \mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}=D_{\Lambda,N}/S_N,$$
where the permutation group $S_N$ acts by relabelling coordinates. Give $\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}$ the quotient sigma-algebra: $A\subseteq\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}$ is measurable exactly when its preimage under the quotient map $q_N:D_{\Lambda,N}\to\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}$ is measurable in the trace of the completed product-Lebesgue sigma-algebra. Identify each orbit with its unordered simple configuration. For $N=0$, set $\mathcal C_{\Lambda,0}=\{\varnothing\}$. If $\lambda_{\Lambda}^{\otimes N}$ is product Lebesgue measure restricted to $D_{\Lambda,N}$, define the sector reference measure by
$$\mu_{\Lambda,N}=\frac1{N!}(q_N)_\#\lambda_{\Lambda}^{\otimes N}\quad(N\geq1),\qquad \mu_{\Lambda,0}(\{\varnothing\})=1.$$
Equivalently, for every nonnegative measurable function $f$ on $\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}$,
$$\int f(\omega)\,\mu_{\Lambda,N}(d\omega)=\frac1{N!}\int_{D_{\Lambda,N}}f(q_N(x_1,\ldots,x_N))\,d^{dN}x.$$
Collision diagonals have product Lebesgue measure zero, so $\mu_{\Lambda,N}(\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N})=|\Lambda|^N/N!$; in particular, symmetric integrands may use the equivalent integral over all of $\Lambda^N$. Thus $\mu_{\Lambda,N}$ is a finite measure, not generally a probability. Two labelled tuples represent the same state exactly when they are in one $S_N$ orbit. The factor $1/N!$ is an adopted indistinguishable-particle positional convention, not a theorem about classical trajectories or every classical description.

Let $\mathcal C_\Lambda=\bigsqcup_{N\geq0}\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}$ with the disjoint-union sigma-algebra, and regard each $\mu_{\Lambda,N}$ as a measure on this union supported on its $N$-point sector. Define the unit-intensity finite-region Poisson reference by
$$Q_\Lambda=e^{-|\Lambda|}\sum_{N=0}^{\infty}\mu_{\Lambda,N}.$$
Its total mass is one because $\mu_{\Lambda,N}(\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N})=|\Lambda|^N/N!$ and $e^{-|\Lambda|}\sum_{N\geq0}|\Lambda|^N/N!=1$. This is a positional reference measure in the chosen dimensionless coordinates; it supplies no empirical claim about particle trajectories.

items.physical_scope: Classical models of identical point particles of one species represented only by their positions in a fixed finite spatial region; it does not assert quantum statistics or include momentum states.

items.title: Exact-particle-number positional energy shell
items.statement:
Use $\Lambda_n=[-n-\tfrac12,n+\tfrac12)^d$, its side length $L_n=2n+1$ and dimensionless volume $V_n=L_n^d$, the periodic positional energy $H_{L_n,\mathrm{per}}$ of [[def-td-stable-tempered-continuum-preparation]], and the exact-$N$ measure $\mu_{\Lambda_n,N}$ of [[post-td-classical-indistinguishable-particle-measure]]. Given $N_n\in\mathbb N_0$, a reduced configuration-energy center $e\in\mathbb R$ joules per dimensionless reference volume, and a width $\delta_n>0$ in the same units, define
$$S_n(N_n,e,\delta_n)=\{\omega\subset\Lambda_n:|\omega|=N_n,\ |H_{L_n,\mathrm{per}}(\omega)/V_n-e|\leq\delta_n\}.$$
When $0<\mu_{\Lambda_n,N_n}(S_n)<\infty$, the uniform positional shell law is
$$M_n(A)=\frac{\mu_{\Lambda_n,N_n}(A\cap S_n)}{\mu_{\Lambda_n,N_n}(S_n)}.$$
A shrinking energy-density shell uses some specified sequence $\delta_n\downarrow0$. Its total energy width is $2\delta_nV_n$, which is $o(V_n)$ but need not be microscopic or bounded. Existence of a normalizing shell and the existence of a suitable shrinking sequence are separate theorem obligations. This is not a surface measure on an exact-energy hypersurface and not a phase-space shell for $K(p)+H_N^{\mathrm{per}}$.

items.physical_scope: Finite periodic boxes of the classical pair-potential positional model; shells constrain pair configuration energy only and exclude kinetic momentum energy.

items.title: Retained hard-core continuation at zero inverse temperature
items.statement:
For the pair potential $\varphi$ of [[def-td-stable-tempered-continuum-preparation]], let $B=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:\varphi(x)=+\infty\}$. A finite configuration is hard-admissible if every pair displacement avoids $B$. For $z>0$, define the retained-admissibility zero-inverse-temperature free-wall weight of $\omega$ to be
$$w_0(\omega)=z^{N(\omega)}\mathbf 1_{\{H_{N(\omega)}(\omega)<\infty\}}.$$
Its finite-volume partition sum, when finite, is $\Xi_{\Lambda}^{\mathrm{ret},0}(z)=\sum_{N\geq0}\int w_0(\omega)\,\mu_{\Lambda,N}(d\omega)$, using [[post-td-classical-indistinguishable-particle-measure]]. This definition sets the weight of a forbidden configuration to zero; it does not assign a value to the undefined product $0\cdot(+\infty)$. When $B=\varnothing$ the measure is the unrestricted Poisson activity model; for a nonempty hard core it is generally not Poisson. The convention is explicit model data and carries no statement about an arbitrary zero-width energy shell.

For a periodic cell of side $L$ in dimensionless coordinates, use the exact image energy $H_{L,\mathrm{per}}$ of [[def-td-stable-tempered-continuum-preparation]]. Its periodic retained-admissibility weight is
$$w_{L,0}^{\mathrm{per}}(\omega)=z^{N(\omega)}\mathbf1_{\{H_{L,\mathrm{per}}(\omega)<+\infty\}}=z^{N(\omega)}\mathbf1_{\{\varphi(y-x)<+\infty\text{ for every }x\in\omega,\ y\in\omega^{\mathrm{per}},\ y\ne x\}}.$$
Thus every forbidden pair between distinct particles and every forbidden periodic-image pair, including a particle with one of its own nontrivial images, receives zero weight. When finite, the corresponding partition sum is $\Xi_{L}^{\mathrm{ret},0,\mathrm{per}}(z)=\sum_{N\geq0}\int w_{L,0}^{\mathrm{per}}\,d\mu_{\Lambda_L,N}$. This is the periodic retained-admissibility convention; it is not an unrestricted zero-beta limit of a shell law.

items.physical_scope: Finite-volume positional models with forbidden pair separations; this is a declared beta-zero hard-admissibility continuation, not a claim about all infinite-temperature physical preparations.

items.title: Finite-volume equilibrium ensemble sampling
items.statement:
For a specified finite region and free or periodic boundary preparation, take $T>0$, $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$ with the SI conventions of [[def-td-stable-tempered-continuum-preparation]], and the corresponding positional energy. Write $H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{free}}=H_N$ for a free region and, for a periodic cube $\Lambda_L$, write $H_{\Lambda_L,N}^{\mathrm{per}}=H_{L,\mathrm{per}}$; in each case $N=N(\omega)$. Set $\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{fin}}=\{\omega\in\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}:H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}(\omega)<+\infty\}$. This set is measurable because the pair potential is measurable and the periodic energy is a countable sum of measurable image terms. On it $H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}$ is real-valued. Specialize the measurable-model canonical preparation of [[post-td-canonical-sampling]] to this set with reference measure $\mu_{\Lambda,N}$ restricted to it; adopt
$$Z_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}=\int_{\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{fin}}}e^{-\beta H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}(\omega)}\,\mu_{\Lambda,N}(d\omega),\qquad P_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{can}}(d\omega)=\frac{\mathbf1_{\mathcal C_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{fin}}}(\omega)e^{-\beta H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}(\omega)}}{Z_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}}\,\mu_{\Lambda,N}(d\omega),$$
whenever $0<Z_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}<\infty$. Define the Boltzmann factor to be zero on configurations with energy $+\infty$; thus no value of an exponential at $+\infty$ is needed. Separately adopt the grand-canonical law at activity $z>0$ to have weights $z^Ne^{-\beta H_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}}$ on the finite-energy part of each sector and zero elsewhere, relative to the same indistinguishable positional measures. Its normalizer is $\Xi_\Lambda(z,\beta)=\sum_{N\geq0}z^NZ_{\Lambda,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}$ when finite. Here $z$ is dimensionless relative to the reference intensity in [[post-td-classical-indistinguishable-particle-measure]], and $\alpha=\log z$.

For the controlled positional shell of [[def-td-controlled-fixed-n-energy-shell]], adopt the conditional measure $M_n$ only when its shell has positive finite reference measure. These are probability-law preparations used to define the model. They are not derived from Hamiltonian trajectories, and they do not assert that a laboratory apparatus reaches any of them. The inverse-temperature-zero hard-core continuation is governed separately by [[def-td-retained-hard-core-zero-beta-preparation]].

items.physical_scope: Adopted canonical, grand-canonical, and positional microcanonical preparations of a classical pair-potential model in a stated finite region; no dynamical relaxation, ergodicity, or empirical thermalization is asserted.

items.title: Selected grand-variational phase uniqueness
items.statement:
Fix the selected stable regularly tempered pair model with Borel-measurable $\widehat\varphi=\varphi/E_0$, $T>0$, $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$ with the SI conventions of [[def-td-stable-tempered-continuum-preparation]], and activity $z>0$. For the superstable branch, require measurable even pair potentials $\varphi_s,\varphi_r$ with $\varphi=\varphi_s+\varphi_r$, where $\varphi_s$ is stable in joules and $\varphi_r(x)\geq0$ joules for every $x$. Require constants $\epsilon>0$ joules and $r_0>0$ in dimensionless coordinates such that $\varphi_r(x)\geq\epsilon$ whenever $\|x\|_\infty\leq r_0$, where $\|x\|_\infty=\max_j|x_j|$. After energy conversion, $\widehat\varphi_s=\varphi_s/E_0$ is stable and $\widehat\varphi_r=\varphi_r/E_0\geq0$ with core lower bound $\epsilon/E_0$, exactly as in [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]. This is an additional model hypothesis, not a consequence of stability alone.

Under the Axiom of Choice, use the global measurable configuration space $\Omega$ of [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]], consisting of locally finite simple configurations with sigma-algebra generated by bounded-Borel count maps. For $a\in\mathbb R^d$, let $T_a\omega(A)=\omega(A-a)$ be its measurable translation. A probability law $P$ on $\Omega$ is stationary exactly when $P\circ T_a^{-1}=P$ for every $a\in\mathbb R^d$. For a bounded Borel region $A$, equip its finite simple configuration set $\mathcal C_A$ with $\mathcal F_A^{\rm count}=\sigma(N_B:B\subseteq A\text{ Borel})$, without completing it. On this space $r_A(\omega)=\omega\cap A$ is measurable: each generating count satisfies $N_B\circ r_A=N_B$, a bounded-Borel global count. Write $P_A=P\circ r_A^{-1}$ on this exact count sigma-algebra for every stationary $P$. This assertion does not extend $P_A$ to the completed quotient sigma-algebra. The reference $Q_A=Q\circ r_A^{-1}$ is the restriction of the same unit-intensity law $Q$; by [[thm-tdmath-poisson-reference-count-properties]] and the count-generated restriction sigma-algebra, it equals the restriction to $\mathcal F_A^{\rm count}$ of the finite-sector law $e^{-|A|}\sum_{N\geq0}\mu_{A,N}$ of [[post-td-classical-indistinguishable-particle-measure]]. This count sigma-algebra is contained in the completed quotient sigma-algebra: in each sector, the pullback of $N_B$ is $\sum_{j=1}^N\mathbf1_B(x_j)$, a Borel function, so each count generator is quotient measurable. Thus the stated restriction of the positional measure is defined. Relative entropy and the restrictions below always use $\mathcal F_A^{\rm count}$, exactly as in the mathematical global supplier, rather than an unproved completion for arbitrary $P$. Indeed, a finite Borel partition of $A$ has multinomial counts under each fixed-$N$ Lebesgue sector, and summing these sector measures with the factor $e^{-|A|}$ gives independent Poisson counts of the corresponding volumes. For each bounded Borel $A$, write $D_A(P)=D(P_A\|Q_A)$ using [[def-tdmath-finite-region-relative-entropy]]: if $P_A\ll Q_A$ and $h_A=dP_A/dQ_A$, then $D_A(P)=\int h_A\log h_A\,dQ_A$ with $0\log0=0$; otherwise $D_A(P)=+\infty$. Let $C_0=[0,1)^d$ and $\Lambda_L=[0,L)^d$. Define $\rho(P)=E_PN_{C_0}$ and let $\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}$ be the stationary laws with finite intensity $\rho(P)<\infty$. For $P\in\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}$ for which both limits exist and are finite, define
$$
I(P)=\lim_{L\to\infty}\frac{D_{\Lambda_L}(P)}{|\Lambda_L|},\qquad \Phi(P)=\lim_{L\to\infty}\frac{E_P[H_{\Lambda_L}^{\mathrm{free}}]}{|\Lambda_L|}.
$$
Here $I(P)$ and $\rho(P)$ are dimensionless per dimensionless reference volume; the physical number density corresponding to $\rho(P)$ is $\rho(P)/\ell_0^d$ in $\mathrm{m}^{-d}$. The energy density $\Phi(P)$ is in joules per dimensionless reference volume; the corresponding energy density per physical $d$-volume is $\Phi(P)/\ell_0^d$ in $\mathrm{J\,m^{-d}}$.
For $\beta>0$, use the laws $P\in\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}$ with finite $I(P)$ and $\Phi(P)$ and adopt, at the selected $(\varphi,\beta,z)$, that
$$\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{P}\{I(P)+\beta\Phi(P)-\rho(P)\log z\}=\{P^\ast\}.$$

For the $\beta=0$ branch, require a nonempty hard-core displacement set $B=\{x:\varphi(x)=+\infty\}$ and use [[def-td-retained-hard-core-zero-beta-preparation]]. A global configuration is hard-admissible when no pair of its distinct points has displacement in $B$. Restrict to $P\in\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}$ assigning probability one to hard-admissible configurations and having finite $I(P)$; adopt, at the selected $z$, that
$$\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{P}\{I(P)-\rho(P)\log z\}=\{P^\ast\}.$$
These are two explicit parameter-specific physical model restrictions. They do not assert uniqueness for every activity or temperature, do not apply at coexistence when the minimizer set has several elements, and do not infer uniqueness from thermodynamic smoothness.

items.physical_scope: Only a named Borel-measurable stable regularly tempered model and parameter point on the positive-temperature branch or explicitly retained hard-core beta-zero branch for which the corresponding translation-invariant variational minimizer is assumed unique; no universal uniqueness or claim at coexistence.

items.title: Stable-tempered free-cube grand pressure
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $d\geq2$, $\varphi$ be stable with the regular integrable tail of [[def-td-stable-tempered-continuum-preparation]], and assume its dimensionless representative $\widehat\varphi=\varphi/E_0$ is Borel measurable, as required by the current mathematical supplier. Take $T>0$ and $z>0$ as in [[post-td-equilibrium-ensemble-sampling]], set $E_0=1\,\mathrm J$, $\beta=(k_BT)^{-1}$, and $\widehat\beta=E_0\beta>0$. For cubes $\Lambda_L=[-L/2,L/2)^d$, let $\Xi_L(z,\beta)$ be the free-wall grand partition function specified by [[post-td-equilibrium-ensemble-sampling]]. Then the positional grand pressure per physical $d$-volume
$p_L(z,T)=\frac{k_BT}{\ell_0^d|\Lambda_L|}\log\Xi_L(z,\beta)$
has a finite limit as $L\to\infty$. Its units are $\mathrm{J\,m^{-d}}$; for $d=3$ this is SI pressure in pascals. In the dimensionless reference-volume convention of [[thm-tdmath-canonical-grand-duality]], let $P(\alpha,\widehat\beta)=\lim_{L\to\infty}|\Lambda_L|^{-1}\log\Xi_L(e^\alpha,\widehat\beta)$, where the supplier uses numerical energies in units of $E_0$. Then $p=(k_BT/\ell_0^d)P(\log z,\widehat\beta)$. This is a conditional model deduction, not a measurement or an assertion that every real gas realizes the preparation.

items.physical_scope: Positive-temperature grand-canonical positional preparations in cubic free-wall boxes for stable even Borel pair potentials with the explicitly stated decreasing integrable tail.

items.title: Controlled continuum interval-energy thermodynamic limit
items.statement:
Assume AC, the ultrafilter extension principle, DC, and HB, as required by the current variational-pressure supplier. Let $E_0=1\,\mathrm J$, $\widehat\varphi=\varphi/E_0$, and assume $\widehat\varphi$ is Borel measurable. Require the exact superstable regular hypotheses of [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]] for this dimensionless potential: a stable part plus a nonnegative core part bounded below by a positive constant on an $\ell^\infty$-ball, with the supplier's lower and upper regular tail conditions. Use $\widehat H=H/E_0$; then $\widehat\beta\widehat H=\beta H$ when $\widehat\beta=E_0\beta$.

Use the stationary finite-intensity law space $\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}$ and the supplier's $\rho(P)$ (expected count in a dimensionless unit cube), $I(P)$ (specific relative entropy against the unit-intensity Poisson law), and $\widehat\Phi(P)$ (limiting numerical positional energy density) from [[thm-tdmath-continuum-variational-pressure]]. Define
$$\nu=\sup\{\rho(P):P\in\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat},\ I(P)<\infty,\ \widehat\Phi(P)<\infty\},\qquad e_0(\rho)=\inf\{\widehat\Phi(P):P\in\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat},\ \rho(P)=\rho,\ I(P)<\infty\},$$
with the supremum of an empty set equal to $0$ and the infimum of an empty set equal to $+\infty$. Here $\rho$ is particle count per dimensionless reference volume, corresponding to physical number density $\rho/\ell_0^d$ in $\mathrm{m}^{-d}$. Let $D\subset[0,\infty)$ be an interval of positive length and let $\widehat e\in\mathbb R$ be a numerical energy per dimensionless reference volume. Require $\inf D<\nu$ and $\widehat e>\inf_{\rho\in D}e_0(\rho)$, and set $e=E_0\widehat e$ in joules per dimensionless reference volume. The interval-event supplier [[thm-tdmath-interval-event-ensemble-limit]] supplies a multiplier pair $(\widehat\beta,z)$ with $\widehat\beta\geq0$ and $z>0$ for this same $(D,\widehat e)$. If $\widehat\beta>0$, take $\beta=\widehat\beta/E_0$ in $\mathrm{J}^{-1}$ and $T=E_0/(k_{\mathrm B}\widehat\beta)>0$ in kelvins. If $\widehat\beta=0$, use only the formal retained-hard-admissibility branch below; it is not a finite-temperature preparation.

For integers $n\geq0$, set $L_n=2n+1$, $\Lambda_n=[-L_n/2,L_n/2)^d$, and $V_n=|\Lambda_n|=L_n^d$. Define
$$A_n=\{\omega:N_{\Lambda_n}(\omega)/V_n\in D,\ H_{L_n,\mathrm{per}}(\omega)/(E_0V_n)\leq\widehat e\},$$
where $H_{L_n,\mathrm{per}}$ is the physical positional energy in joules with the image convention of [[def-td-stable-tempered-continuum-preparation]]. Equivalently, the upper-energy event is $H_{L_n,\mathrm{per}}/V_n\leq e$. For each $n$ with positive event probability, set $R_n(B)=Q_{\Lambda_n}(B\cap A_n)/Q_{\Lambda_n}(A_n)$ on the finite count sigma-algebra. Equivalently, with $M_n=\sum_{N\geq0}\mu_{\Lambda_n,N}$, $R_n(B)=M_n(B\cap A_n)/M_n(A_n)$, since $Q_{\Lambda_n}=e^{-V_n}M_n$; use the count-sigma restriction of these positional measures. This defines the density-interval/upper-energy conditional preparation.

For the positive-$\widehat\beta$ branch, the finite-volume grand and conditional laws use the adopted positional preparation of [[post-td-equilibrium-ensemble-sampling]] at the matching $T$ and $z$. For the $\widehat\beta=0$ branch, require a nonempty hard-core displacement set $B=\{x:\varphi(x)=+\infty\}$ and use the formal retained-admissibility continuation of [[def-td-retained-hard-core-zero-beta-preparation]]; do not interpret $0\cdot(+\infty)$. Assume the singleton-minimizer postulate [[post-td-grand-variational-phase-uniqueness]] holds on its stated finite-intensity stationary-law domain at this exact supplier-selected multiplier pair and branch.

For either branch, [[thm-tdmath-interval-event-ensemble-limit]] gives eventual event positivity, the constrained entropy-rate limit, and common-minimizer accumulation points; at $\widehat\beta=0$, [[thm-tdmath-retained-hard-zero-beta-limit]] identifies the matching retained grand law and minimizer set. Under the stated singleton assumption, both the conditioned laws and the corresponding periodic grand laws converge locally to $P^*$ for every measurable local observable $f$ supported in a bounded region $A$ and satisfying $|f|\leq c(1+N_A)$. The energy-density center $e$ and widths for this model are in joules per dimensionless reference volume; the corresponding physical $d$-volume density has units $\mathrm{J\,m^{-d}}$. This is an interval-density and upper-energy result, not a fixed-particle-number or shrinking-shell theorem.

Here local observables are evaluated on the periodic continuation of the prepared torus configuration. This is the same periodic boundary preparation, with no new physical sampling assumption; a configuration is not extended by the empty configuration outside its fundamental cube.

items.title: Controlled canonical–grand thermodynamic duality
items.statement:
Assume AC and $T>0$, with $\beta=(k_BT)^{-1}$, and take $z>0$ as in [[post-td-equilibrium-ensemble-sampling]]. Under the stable regularly tempered positional model of [[def-td-stable-tempered-continuum-preparation]] and the adopted ensemble weights of [[post-td-equilibrium-ensemble-sampling]], assume the dimensionless potential $\widehat\varphi=\varphi/E_0$ is Borel measurable as required by the current mathematical carriers. Set $E_0=1\,\mathrm J$ and $\widehat\beta=E_0\beta$; write $F(\rho,\beta)$ and $P(\alpha,\beta)$ for the mathematical rates evaluated at $\widehat\beta$. Let $F(\rho,\beta)$ be the canonical log-partition rate per dimensionless reference volume, defined on interior attainable densities by the fixed-density limit and extended to the closed effective density domain by the upper-semicontinuous concave extension specified in [[thm-tdmath-canonical-grand-duality]], with $F(\rho,\beta)=-\infty$ outside that closed domain. Let
$$P(\alpha,\beta)=\lim_{V\to\infty}V^{-1}\log\sum_{N\geq0}e^{\alpha N}Z(V,N),\qquad \alpha=\log z.$$
Then
$$P(\alpha,\beta)=\sup_{\rho\geq0}\{F(\rho,\beta)+\alpha\rho\},$$
and, for every $\rho$ in the closed effective density domain of $F$,
$$F(\rho,\beta)=\inf_{\alpha\in\mathbb R}\{P(\alpha,\beta)-\alpha\rho\}.$$
The density $\rho$ is particle count per dimensionless reference volume, corresponding to physical number density $\rho/\ell_0^d$ in $\mathrm{m}^{-d}$. In physical units, $p=(k_BT/\ell_0^d)P$ and the positional Helmholtz free-energy density is $f_{\mathrm{pos}}=-(k_BT/\ell_0^d)F$; both are per physical $d$-volume, in $\mathrm{J\,m^{-d}}$ (pascals when $d=3$). The fixed $1/N!$ reference normalization is that of [[post-td-classical-indistinguishable-particle-measure]]. This duality concerns limiting thermodynamic functions only. It does not imply local ensemble equivalence, uniqueness of a phase, or convergence at excluded density endpoints.

items.title: Interacting exact-N shrinking-shell three-ensemble local limit
items.statement:
Assume AC, the ultrafilter extension principle, DC, and HB as required by the current variational-pressure supplier. Take $T>0$ in kelvins and $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$ in $\mathrm{J}^{-1}$ as in [[post-td-equilibrium-ensemble-sampling]]. Let $E_0=1\,\mathrm J$, $\widehat\varphi=\varphi/E_0$, and assume $\widehat\varphi$ is Borel measurable. Require the exact superstable regular hypotheses of [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]; use $\widehat H=H/E_0$ and $\widehat\beta=E_0\beta>0$ in its mathematical suppliers. Let $F(\rho,\beta)$ denote the dimensionless canonical log-partition rate per dimensionless reference volume evaluated at $\widehat\beta$. Assume it is differentiable in physical $\beta$ at the chosen temperature and set $e=-\partial_\beta F(\rho,\beta)$, in joules per dimensionless reference volume. For periodic cubes $\Lambda_n$, take exact particle numbers $N_n$ with $N_n/V_n\to\rho$ at a positive interior attainable density; $\rho$ is particle count per dimensionless reference volume, corresponding to physical number density $\rho/\ell_0^d$ in $\mathrm{m}^{-d}$. Choose $\alpha\in\mathbb R$ such that $F(s,\beta)+\alpha s\leq F(\rho,\beta)+\alpha\rho$ for every $s$ in the closed effective density domain of $F$, and set $z=e^\alpha>0$. Assume the corresponding stationary finite-intensity grand variational minimizer is the singleton $P^\ast$ as in [[post-td-grand-variational-phase-uniqueness]].

Then there exists a constructed sequence $\delta_n\downarrow0$ for which the periodic exact-$N_n$ canonical positional law, the periodic grand-canonical law at $(\alpha,\beta)$, and the uniform positional shell law of [[def-td-controlled-fixed-n-energy-shell]] on
$$N=N_n,\qquad |H_{L_n,\mathrm{per}}/V_n-e|\leq\delta_n,\qquad L_n=2n+1$$
all converge locally to $P^\ast$. Convergence means convergence of expectations for every measurable local observable $f$ supported in a bounded region and satisfying $|f|\leq c(1+N_A)$ there. The shell sequence is constructed from canonical concentration; each $\delta_n$ is in joules per dimensionless reference volume, corresponding to physical energy-density width $\delta_n/\ell_0^d$ in $\mathrm{J\,m^{-d}}$. Arbitrary preassigned shrinking widths, exact zero-width surfaces, full phase-space shells involving kinetic momentum, and a conclusion at nonunique minimizers are not asserted.

Here local observables are evaluated on the periodic continuation of the prepared torus configuration. This is the same periodic boundary preparation, with no new physical sampling assumption; a configuration is not extended by the empty configuration outside its fundamental cube.

items.title: Qualified van Hove and tempered-exterior thermodynamic limits
items.statement:
Assume AC, as required by the current mathematical definition and its shape suppliers. Let $d\geq2$, $E_0=1\,\mathrm J$, $\widehat\varphi=\varphi/E_0$, and assume $\widehat\varphi$ is Borel measurable and superstable and regular as in [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]. Use $\widehat H=H/E_0$ and $\widehat\beta=E_0(k_BT)^{-1}>0$ in the mathematical rates. Let $(\Lambda_k)$ be a van Hove sequence as in [[def-td-admissible-van-hove-and-tempered-exterior]]. First, for free walls, the positional grand pressure along $\Lambda_k$ converges to the free-cube pressure of [[pthm-td-stable-tempered-free-cube-grand-pressure]]. For any positive interior attainable density $\rho$ (particle count per dimensionless reference volume, with physical density $\rho/\ell_0^d$ in $\mathrm{m}^{-d}$) and exact integers $N_k$ with $N_k/|\Lambda_k|\to\rho$, the exact-$N_k$ free-wall canonical log-partition rate converges to the same cube canonical rate. These two shape statements require superstability and regularity; stability alone is not asserted to suffice for arbitrary van Hove shapes.

Second, strengthen the potential hypothesis: for some $r_0>0$, $\widehat\varphi(x)\geq\widehat\chi(\|x\|_\infty)>0$ whenever $0<\|x\|_\infty\leq r_0$, where $\widehat\chi:(0,r_0]\to(0,\infty)$ is finite-valued and nonincreasing and $\int_0^{r_0}\widehat\chi(r)r^{d-1}\,dr=+\infty$. For each fixed $0\leq t<\infty$, the free-wall grand pressure in $\Lambda_n$ with exterior $\zeta\in\Omega(t)$ then converges uniformly in $\zeta$ to the same free-cube pressure. The exterior interaction is the deterministic positional term of [[def-td-admissible-van-hove-and-tempered-exterior]], not a volume-filling external field. This genuine divergent-core condition is the exact stronger hypothesis of the current exterior supplier; it is not inferred from superstability or replaced by a weaker source condition.

items.title: Two indistinguishable hard-core particles in an interval
items.statement:
Take a dimensionless interval $\Lambda=[0,L]$ with $0<a<L$, two identical particles, and the hard-core pair potential $\varphi(r)=+\infty$ for $|r|<a$ and $0$ otherwise. At any positive temperature the configurational canonical partition function is independent of $T$ and equals
$$Z_{\Lambda,2}=\frac12(L-a)^2.$$
The factor $1/2$ is the adopted indistinguishable positional measure. This finite-volume calculation has no momentum variables or experimental data.
items.physical_scope: A finite one-dimensional positional toy model with two classical identical particles and a hard-core exclusion; it is a model calculation, not a reported measurement.

items.title: Two minimizers in a reduced coexistence model
items.statement: Consider the reduced coarse-grained variational model with scalar dimensionless order parameter $m\in[-1,1]$ and dimensionless free-energy function $g(m)=(m^2-1)^2$. Its global minimizers are $m=-1$ and $m=1$. This model shows why uniqueness must be stated as a parameter-specific assumption. It does not identify these two minimizers with Gibbs measures of a continuum pair potential.
items.physical_scope: A dimensionless coarse-grained order-parameter example illustrating a possible failure of a singleton variational-minimizer assumption; it is not a continuum Gibbs-potential calculation.

items.title: Hard-core exclusion retained at zero inverse temperature
items.statement: In an interval $\Lambda=[0,L]$, let two particles have hard-core radius $a$ with $0<a<L$. Under the retained-admissibility zero-inverse-temperature preparation, the weight is zero on $|x_1-x_2|<a$ and equals $z^2$ on $|x_1-x_2|\geq a$. Hence this law is not the unrestricted Poisson activity law, which assigns positive mass to the forbidden band. The conclusion concerns the finite positional continuation defined on the A page.
items.physical_scope: A finite-volume positional hard-core model under the explicitly defined retained-admissibility beta-zero continuation; no universal infinite-temperature claim is made.

items.title: A volume-filling field changes ideal-gas pressure
items.statement: For the ideal positional gas $\varphi=0$ in dimension $d\geq2$ and a bounded measurable region of dimensionless volume $0\leq V<\infty$, take $z>0$ and $T>0$, with $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}>0$ in $\mathrm{J}^{-1}$. The grand partition is $\Xi_V(z,\beta)=e^{zV}$. Now impose a constant external energy $c\in\mathbb R$ joules per particle at every point of the volume, adding $cN$ to the configuration energy and using the same grand weighting convention. The new grand partition is $\Xi_V^{(c)}=e^{ze^{-\beta c}V}$. For $V>0$, the dimensionless per-volume log-partition rate changes from $z$ to $ze^{-\beta c}$ when $c\neq0$. At $V=0$, both partitions are $1$ and no per-volume rate is assigned. For $c\neq0$, this energy shift cannot be represented on the nonempty cubes $\Lambda_n$ by the deterministic exterior interaction used by [[pthm-td-qualified-van-hove-and-exterior-limit]]. For $c=0$, it vanishes and agrees with the empty exterior $\varnothing\in\Omega(0)$ of [[def-td-admissible-van-hove-and-tempered-exterior]]. For every $c$, the ideal potential itself fails the cited theorem's stronger interaction hypotheses.
items.physical_scope: A classical ideal positional gas in dimension d at least two with a constant per-particle external energy throughout the volume; a nonzero shift cannot be represented by a uniformly tempered exterior, while the zero shift agrees with the empty exterior. No empirical observation is asserted.
